summary: AI observability has become a critical discipline as LLM deployments scale, enabling teams to trace prompt behavior, track token costs, detect quality regressions, and attribute spend to users or features. The LLM observability platform market grew to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR, reflecting how central monitoring has become to production GenAI systems. Without robust observability, teams operate blind to latency spikes, runaway API costs, and silent model degradation that can erode both user experience and budget.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain executions, agent steps, prompt versions, and evaluation runs within LangChain and LangGraph workflows
features: Full trace and span capture for LangChain and LangGraph pipelines
Prompt versioning and prompt playground for iteration
Built-in evaluation harnesses with human and automated feedback
Dataset management for regression testing
Cost attribution per trace with per-thousand-token breakdown
Latency and error rate dashboards
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces per month; Plus at $39 per seat per month with overage at approximately $2.50 per thousand traces; at 100,000 traces per month total cost reaches approximately $264 according to LangChain
tools.best_for: Teams already using LangChain or LangGraph who need deep chain-level tracing, prompt management, and integrated evaluation in a single platform

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, response quality, token usage, cost per request, provider latency, and error rates via a lightweight proxy gateway
features: Single base-URL change integration requiring no SDK refactor
Cost tracking across 300+ models using an open model-cost repository
Per-user and per-session spend attribution
Hard budget limits and rate limiting at the gateway level
Prompt templating and caching to reduce redundant API calls
Real-time dashboard for request volume, cost, and latency
tools.pricing: Free tier at 10,000 requests per month; Pro tier reaches 100,000 requests at approximately $79 per month according to Markaicode; consumption-based pricing scales with request volume
tools.best_for: Teams needing instant cost visibility and budget governance in under five minutes without deep SDK integration, especially for multi-model or multi-department spend tracking

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, model evaluation runs, experiment metrics, dataset versions, and end-to-end ML pipeline lineage
features: Weave module for LLM tracing and evaluation layered on top of W&B experiment tracking
Automatic logging of prompts, completions, and metadata
Evaluation dashboards comparing model versions and prompt strategies
Dataset versioning and artifact tracking for reproducibility
Integration with popular frameworks including OpenAI, LangChain, and Hugging Face
Collaborative workspace for team-based experiment review
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Team plans start at $50 per user per month; Enterprise pricing available on request; W&B Weave tracing is included in existing W&B subscriptions
tools.best_for: ML and research teams who already use W&B for experiment tracking and want to extend observability to LLM evaluations and prompt experiments without adopting a separate tool

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: LLM traces, embedding drift, retrieval quality in RAG pipelines, model performance over time, and enterprise-scale telemetry
features: Phoenix open-source tracing library for local and cloud use
RAG pipeline evaluation including context relevance and faithfulness scoring
Embedding visualization and drift detection for semantic shift
Integration with OpenTelemetry for standardized trace ingestion
Online and offline evaluation workflows
Enterprise RBAC, SSO, and data residency controls
tools.pricing: Phoenix is open source and free to self-host; Arize cloud platform offers a free Developer tier; Growth and Enterprise tiers are usage-based with pricing available on request; targets enterprise teams with volume discounts
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams running RAG or embedding-heavy workloads who need production-grade telemetry, semantic drift monitoring, and compliance-ready infrastructure

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, prompt versions, evaluation scores, and token costs across any LLM provider via SDK or OpenTelemetry
features: Open-source core with self-hosting option for full data control
Trace and span capture compatible with OpenAI, Anthropic, and any provider
Prompt management with version history and A/B comparison
User-level and session-level analytics for cost and quality attribution
Native DeepEval and custom evaluation integrations
LLM-as-judge scoring pipelines for automated quality assessment
tools.pricing: Open source and free to self-host with no request limits; Langfuse Cloud Hobby tier free at limited usage; Pro tier at $59 per month for teams; Enterprise plans available with SSO and SLA
tools.best_for: Open-source-first teams or those with data privacy requirements who want full tracing and prompt management without vendor lock-in, especially across heterogeneous LLM providers

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, token usage, latency, and errors via OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation that exports to any compatible observability backend
features: OpenTelemetry-based SDK that auto-instruments OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and other providers
Exports traces and metrics to any OTLP-compatible backend including Datadog, Grafana, Jaeger, and OpenObserve
Zero vendor lock-in by design using open standards
Minimal code changes required for instrumentation
Community-maintained provider integrations updated frequently
Compatible with existing APM stacks without replacing them
tools.pricing: Fully open source under Apache 2.0 license; free to use with no usage caps; costs are only those of the backend you export to
tools.best_for: Platform and DevOps teams who want to add LLM observability to an existing OpenTelemetry-based stack without adopting a new SaaS tool, maintaining a single pane of glass for all telemetry

tools.name: OpenObserve
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt metadata, cost, infrastructure logs, application metrics, and frontend RUM in a single unified deployment
features: Unified platform combining LLM tracing with logs, metrics, traces, and RUM monitoring
Eliminates the need for a separate DevOps telemetry stack alongside an LLM tool
Prompt management and cost tracking built in
OpenTelemetry-compatible ingestion for broad provider support
Self-hostable with a cloud option for teams preferring managed infrastructure
Significantly lower storage costs compared to Elasticsearch-based stacks
tools.pricing: Open source and free to self-host; OpenObserve Cloud offers a free tier; paid cloud plans are consumption-based starting at competitive rates relative to Datadog and similar platforms
tools.best_for: Teams tired of managing separate DevOps and LLM observability stacks who want a single deployment covering infrastructure monitoring and LLM-specific tracing with cost tracking

tools.name: Confident AI
tools.monitors: LLM output quality, evaluation metrics, regression across prompt versions, and real-time online evaluations integrated into the observability layer
features: DeepEval open-source framework with 50+ evaluation metrics including faithfulness, hallucination, and contextual relevance
Used by OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft teams according to Confident AI
Online evaluations running in production alongside traces
Regression dashboards comparing evaluation scores across deployments
Integration with CI/CD pipelines for automated quality gating
Deep RAG evaluation metrics beyond simple retrieval accuracy
tools.pricing: DeepEval is open source and free; Confident AI platform offers a free tier for individuals; Pro and Team plans available with pricing on request; Enterprise plans include SSO and dedicated support
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing output quality and safety over cost monitoring alone, particularly those running RAG pipelines or agentic systems where hallucination and faithfulness metrics are business-critical

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching and request deduplication at the gateway level using tools like Helicone or LiteLLM so that identical or near-identical prompts return cached responses without hitting the model API, which can reduce redundant token spend by 20 to 40 percent on repetitive workloads

Attribute costs at the user, session, feature, and department level from day one using trace metadata so you can identify which pipelines, customers, or prompt templates are responsible for disproportionate spend before costs compound at scale

Right-size model selection by routing simpler classification or extraction tasks to smaller, cheaper models such as GPT-4o Mini or Claude Haiku while reserving frontier models for complex reasoning tasks, using evaluation scores from tools like DeepEval or LangSmith to confirm quality is maintained at the lower tier

Set hard budget limits and rate limits at the gateway layer using tools like Helicone, Portkey, or LiteLLM so that runaway agents, infinite retry loops, or misconfigured prompts cannot exhaust monthly API budgets before a human can intervene
